Assume a Module With a Default Export\\n\\nSuppose you have a module that exports a class by default:\\n\\n```ts\\n// my-lib.ts\\nexport default class MyLib {\\n  greet(name: string): string {\\n    return `Hello, ${name}`;\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 2. Reopening the Module with Declaration Merging**\\n\\nYou **cannot** add or override methods directly on the exported class itself via augmentation.\\nHowever, you can *extend* the class:\\n\\n```ts\\n// augment.d.ts (or any `.ts` file)\\nimport MyLibOriginal from \\\"./my-lib\\\";\\n\\n// Extend the original class (this creates a new class)\\nexport default class MyNewLib extends MyLibOriginal {\\n  sayBye(name: string): string {\\n    return `Goodbye, ${name}`;\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nBut this does **not** update the original module's default export. Using Declaration Merging for Instance Properties**\\n\\nIf you want to **add type information** for new instance properties or methods to the class (for things like prototype patching), you can do something like this:\\n\\n```ts\\n// my-lib-augmentation.d.ts\\nimport MyLib from \\\"./my-lib\\\";\\n\\ndeclare module \\\"./my-lib\\\" {\\n  interface MyLib {\\n    sayBye(name: string): string;\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nAnd then **actually add the method at runtime:**\\n\\n```ts\\nimport MyLib from \\\"./my-lib\\\";\\n\\n(MyLib.prototype as any).sayBye = function(name: string) {\\n  return `Goodbye, ${name}`;\\n};\\n\\nconst lib = new MyLib();\\nconsole.log(lib.sayBye(\\\"World\\\")); // Goodbye, World\\n```\\n\\nIn this way, **the type system recognizes `sayBye`** because of the augmentation, and at runtime, it works since the prototype was modified.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 3. Summary Table\\n\\n| Goal         | How to Do It                         |\\n|--------------|--------------------------------------|\\n| New subclass | `class Sub extends Original { ... }` |\\n| Declaration  | `declare module '...' { interface ... }` |\\n| Default export *override* | Not supported via augmentation; use subclass instead |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## **Full Example**\\n\\n**my-lib.ts:**\\n```ts\\nexport default class MyLib {\\n  greet(name: string): string {\\n    return `Hello, ${name}`;\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**my-lib-augmentation.d.ts:**\\n```ts\\nimport MyLib from \\\"./my-lib\\\";\\n\\ndeclare module \\\"./my-lib\\\" {\\n  interface MyLib {\\n    sayBye(name: string): string;\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**usage.ts:**\\n```ts\\nimport MyLib from \\\"./my-lib\\\";\\nimport \\\"./my-lib-augmentation\\\";\\n\\n(MyLib.prototype as any).sayBye = function(name: string) {\\n  return `Goodbye, ${name}`;\\n};\\n\\nconst lib = new MyLib();\\nconsole.log(lib.greet(\\\"TypeScript\\\")); // Hello, TypeScript\\nconsole.log(lib.sayBye(\\\"TypeScript\\\")); // Goodbye, TypeScript\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## **Key Points**\\n\\n- You **cannot directly augment the default class**'s methods in place via module augmentation.
